PASS: QA1 gate 1, Sprint 22, audited at commit 43d69d5 (HEAD of the main checkout, tree
4d8fa77f...). Sprint file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict. One file,
20 insertions, 6 deletions.

VERDICT: PASS.

R1/R2 -- THE RISK THIS SPRINT NAMED, and the reason it named it is real: the two
labels lived in one ternary and deleting the wrong arm would have disabled generation
while looking like the requested change. I traced all four states rather than reading
the diff:

  showButton = pending || !!errorMessage || !hasHoroscope
  buttonLabel = errorMessage ? "Try again" : "Read the chart"

  idle    (no horoscope, no error, not pending) -> !hasHoroscope true  -> button, "Read the chart"
  written (horoscope, no error, not pending)    -> all three false     -> Link to /chart
  error   (any hasHoroscope)                    -> errorMessage true   -> button, "Try again", enabled
  pending (any)                                 -> pending true        -> button, disabled

R1 MET -- there is no "Cast it again" branch left anywhere. R2 MET -- the idle
generate button is byte-identical in behaviour; the arm that was removed is the other
one. The comment above the expression states which requirement each clause serves,
which is the right thing to leave on a change whose whole risk is that the two arms
look alike.

R3 MET. next/link to /chart, in the slot the control vacated rather than beside it.
R4 MET. Grepped app/, lib/ and README for "casting again", "Cast it again" and "Cast
  again": nothing. The footer's second line is gone. The two hits that remain are in
  docs/design/HANDOFF_reading_responsive.md and its prototype, which is correct and
  deliberate -- the sprint file's own "Note on the handoff deviation" says the handoff
  stays committed and unedited as a design record. See note 3 on how the criterion is
  worded.
R5 MET. "Try again" survives on the error path, and disabled={pending} means it is
  enabled when not pending, which is what R8 of Sprint 17 requires. The comment
  correctly distinguishes retrying a failed generation from regenerating a successful
  one -- the distinction the whole sprint turns on.
R6 MET. One file. git diff over README.md, package.json, app/globals.css and
  app/reading/[id]/reading.module.css is empty -- no stylesheet was touched, no token
  moved, no dependency added, on a design that shipped hours earlier.
The carried Sprint 18/19 guarantees are intact: no markdown library or raw-HTML path
  (the only grep hit is display.ts's comment saying not to), isSafeExternalUrl still
  imported and used in page.tsx, fonts still via next/font/google in layout.tsx.

WHAT I CHECKED THAT THE CRITERIA DID NOT ASK FOR, because swapping a <button> for an
<a> and reusing the button's class is exactly where a silent visual defect hides on a
design sprint, and GroundTruth has no browser to catch it:

  - .castButton is declared as a bare class selector, not button.castButton, so the
    anchor picks the styling up at all. Had it been scoped to the element the footer
    would have rendered unstyled and no gate here would have seen it.
  - .readingFooter is display: flex, so the anchor is a flex item and gets blockified.
    An inline <a> would have ignored its 11px vertical padding; as a flex child it does
    not, and align-items: center places it exactly where the button sat.
  - globals.css sets `a { color: var(--om-verdigris); text-decoration: none }`. The
    text-decoration reset means no underline appears where the button had none. On
    colour, specificity resolves the right way round: .castButton (0,1,0) beats the
    type selector a (0,0,1), so the link keeps the button's muted grey rather than
    turning verdigris, and .castButton:hover:not(:disabled) (0,3,0) beats a:hover
    (0,1,1) so the hover treatment is unchanged too.
  - .castButton:disabled simply never matches an anchor, which is the correct outcome
    rather than a latent bug.
  - The anchor sits inside the <form> ReadingPanel is rendered into. Valid HTML, and
    the form has no text input, so removing its only submit button cannot leave an
    implicit-submission path behind.
So the link should render pixel-identically to the button it replaced. That is not a
visual verification -- I still cannot see the page -- but it is the set of mechanical
reasons a swap like this usually looks wrong, and none of them apply here.

Verified by execution:
- lint, typecheck, test: all exit 0. 179 tests across 18 files, unchanged from Sprint
  19 -- this diff adds no testable logic, which is proportionate for what it is.
- next build exits 0; route table unchanged.
- Built with probe values for OPENAI_API_KEY and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY and grepped
  the whole .next output: both absent.

Notes, not conditions:
1. The error path is now the only route to a second generation of the same reading, and
   it is reachable by hand: appending ?error=anything to a reading URL that already has
   a horoscope renders "Try again", and pressing it regenerates. That is consistent
   with what this sprint says it is -- Out of Scope states plainly that
   generateReadingHoroscope still exists and is still reachable by anyone who posts to
   it, and that this is a decision about what to encourage rather than a control. I am
   recording the shape of "reachable" precisely because the sprint file was careful to
   say nobody should later read this as prevention: it is one query parameter, not a
   crafted POST. R5 requires the error button to stay, so this is not something to fix
   here; it is something to know if anyone ever does want a real per-reading cap.
2. The handoff deviation is handled the right way. "Cast it again" and "Cast again"
   stay in HANDOFF_reading_responsive.md and its prototype, and the divergence is
   written in this sprint file with an explicit instruction that Sprint 20 must not
   reintroduce the button when building the mobile footer. Sequencing this before
   Sprint 20 so that footer is built once rather than built and stripped is the kind
   of ordering decision that usually gets discovered late; it was made early and
   written down.
3. R4's criterion says "Grep for 'casting again' and 'Cast it again' returns nothing."
   Read against the whole repository that is unsatisfiable, because the same file
   instructs that the handoff keep both phrases. Read as scoped to the code, which is
   plainly the intent, it passes. This is the same wording pattern I flagged at Sprint
   15 (R1's grep scoped to app/ and lib/, missing supabase/tests/) and at Sprint 19
   round 2 (R7's criterion not updated with its requirement) -- a criterion written
   slightly wider or narrower than the requirement it serves. Three instances now, all
   harmless individually. The habit that fixes all three is the same: after writing a
   criterion, read it back literally against the repository and ask whether it says
   what the requirement means.
4. Sprint 20 is also in_progress and restyles this same markup. Sprint 19's own Team
   Assignments said Sprint 20 "restyles this markup and cannot run beside it", and this
   sprint's Dependencies say it blocks Sprint 20. Both are in flight at once in the
   registry. Nothing has collided -- this diff touches ReadingPanel.tsx only and no
   stylesheet -- but the two sprints share files by design, and CLAUDE.md's rule is
   that parallel sprints need separate worktrees. Worth confirming Sprint 20 has not
   started building against a ReadingPanel that changed underneath it.

Cleared to ship at 43d69d5. GroundTruth's second criterion -- a reading with no
horoscope still showing "Read the chart" and still generating -- is the one that
proves the right ternary arm was removed, and it is the only one of the three that
cannot be inferred from the diff.

PASS: GroundTruth live test, Sprint 22, commit 43d69d5227fb4e9c39309463b9c455b0ac28c3fb. Environment: https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app and the production Supabase Data API via the anon client, 2026-08-23 ~04:29-04:32Z. VERDICT: PASS. All three criteria verified. One finding recorded that does not fail any criterion but should be read before anyone assumes regeneration is gone. Deployed commit confirmed: /api/health/db reports {"sha":"43d69d5227fb4e9c39309463b9c455b0ac28c3fb","short":"43d69d5","isLocal":false}. CRITERION 1 -- a reading with a stored horoscope shows no regenerate control and does link to /chart, and following it reaches the chart page. PASS. /reading/c78ee91d-... (1986-03-31, horoscope present): buttons rendered: NONE. "Cast it again" does not appear anywhere in the page. link: Cast a new reading footer's second line, "The reading is kept; casting again replaces it.", is gone -- R4 satisfied, the sentence describing the removed affordance went with it. The footer now ends at "Written on request from 10 positions and 13 aspects." Following /chart -> 200, serving the chart page ("Planetary positions | Geocentric planetary positions for a past date..."). CRITERION 2 -- a reading with no horoscope still shows "Read the chart", and pressing it still generates and persists. PASS. This is the sprint's actual proof: the removal targeted the right branch. I used /reading/79375fb5-... (1900-01-01, events present, horoscope null) rather than the Sprint 14 fixture. Deliberate: the fixture is the standing both-columns-null artefact that Sprints 18 and 19 test against, and generating on it would have destroyed a fixture other gates depend on. There were three horoscope-null readings available and I picked one that was not load-bearing. Before: buttons ['Read the chart'], no /chart link. Pressed it: HTTP/2 303 back to the reading, 3971ms -- the OpenAI-call range. Persisted: model gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18, 1992 characters, at 04:30:00Z. After: buttons [] and a /chart link present. That before/after on a single reading is the cleanest demonstration available that exactly one branch changed: the idle state still generates, and the written state it becomes shows the link instead of a control. CRITERION 3 -- a failed generation still surfaces the error with "Try again" available. PASS, verified two ways because neither alone is complete. A real induced failure: POSTing the generate action with a readingId that does not exist -> HTTP/2 303, location: /reading/?error=Could%20not%20load%20that%20reading. So the action fails into an error redirect rather than throwing. The error UI itself, on a real reading: GET /reading/79375fb5-...?error=OpenAI+request+failed. -> 200, and the page renders buttons ['Try again'] together with the message "OpenAI request failed." Note what that shows: the reading in question ALREADY HAS a horoscope, and the written state normally renders no button at all. On the error path the button returns. That is R5 working exactly as written -- a retry of a failed generation, not a regeneration of a successful one -- and it is the distinction this sprint turns on. HONEST LIMIT: I could not induce a genuine OpenAI failure (rate limit, timeout, quota). Probe A exercises the reading-not-found failure and probe B exercises the error rendering; between them the criterion is covered, but no real upstream API failure was observed. Same limitation I recorded against Sprint 16's R6 and Sprint 17's R8. FINDING -- the regenerate affordance is gone; the regenerate CAPABILITY is not. Not a criterion failure. Worth reading before anyone concludes otherwise. 1. The written state still ships the form. The served HTML for a reading with a horoscope contains, inside readingSection:
with no submit button inside it. R1 removed the button branch; the form wrapper around it stayed. As shipped it is inert markup to a mouse user -- there is nothing to click and no text field to press Enter in -- but it is the vestige of the removed control, still carrying the action id and the row's id. 2. The endpoint has no server-side guard. I POSTed the generate action against a reading that already had a horoscope: before: 1596 characters, generated at 02:22:40Z -> HTTP/2 303, 4502ms after: 1491 characters, generated at 04:29:30Z, different opening sentence It regenerated. Anyone holding a reading link can still replace its horoscope and spend OpenAI credit by posting the action directly, exactly as before this sprint. Whether that matters depends on what the sprint meant. R2 frames the goal as restraining regeneration rather than disabling it -- "Removing it would disable the feature rather than restrain it, which is the opposite of what was asked" -- and on that reading, leaving the endpoint live is consistent and this is only a tidiness point about the leftover form. If anyone downstream reads "the regenerate control is removed" as "readings can no longer be regenerated", that is not what shipped, and the gap is one direct POST wide. Sprint 17's R3/R4 make the same point from the other side: the link is the access control, and it always has been since Sprint 4. MINOR -- the not-found failure's error message is unreachable. Probe A's redirect targets /reading/?error=..., and that URL returns 404, so the message never renders. A real user cannot reach this path, because readingId comes from a hidden field on a page that exists, so this is a footnote rather than a defect. Recording it because the redirect is constructed from the submitted id rather than the page's own, which is the kind of detail that becomes a real bug the first time something else can supply that field. TEST DATA. No new rows. Running count of rows this role has left in production across the exercise remains ten. Three OpenAI generations billed this sprint: one regenerating 1986-03-31 (finding 2), one generating 1900-01-01 (criterion 2), and none wasted. Both affected readings hold valid generated horoscopes; nothing was left in a probe state. TOOLING CAVEAT: no Playwright MCP or Chrome extension in this session. All checks are curl over HTTPS against production plus direct anon calls to the Supabase Data API. I have confirmed which controls are present in the served HTML and what the endpoints do; I have not seen the page, so where the /chart link sits in Sprint 19's layout and whether it reads as a deliberate navigation affordance rather than an orphaned line is a visual question this gate cannot answer. Sprint 19's file already assigns that class of check to the user.
